title: A background `merge --lane-lint` is reported stalled while it runs
why: On 2026-11-08 04:06 CST two background runs of `merge --lane-lint 1497 > $D/lanelint-1497.log 2>&1` ended exit 3 after 300 s, while the lint ran on orphaned; its verdict reached the session only through a later wait-pid. Cause (read): hooks/stall_watch.py named_logs passes each redirect target as `--also F`, and a target written with a shell variable cannot be resolved, so the watcher saw no output. bin/verdict writes a STALL_WATCH_BEAT heartbeat; merge --lane-lint writes none.
note: Fix: merge --lane-lint appends a heartbeat to $STALL_WATCH_BEAT at each suite start, red test first. Not `| tee`: a pipe returns tee's exit (decision verdict-pipe-refused). Possible overlap: PR #1823 (step stall-watch-quiet-lint) adds a beat to the lane-lint wrapper; the lane checks it before building. Coordinator item 386 (04:31 CST Nov 8). Queue fix (owner 13:20 CST Nov 7). Filed 04:33 CST Nov 8; lane notes-fix-report builds it. Folded into stall-watch-quiet-lint: #1823 makes ci-job, which merge --lane-lint runs, append each step start to $STALL_WATCH_BEAT (lane notes-fix-report, 04:33 CST Nov 8). Done with no change; branch lane-lint-beat opens no PR. Session session_013NEJL2qBDyNbgXYNEhpSrf now runs lane notes-fix-report, with 8 PRs handed to runner 8 still unmerged (e.g. #2137) (coordinator 22:12 CST Nov 8); keep it open.
